entry.title: Extending SAP Document and Reporting Compliance for Paraguay: an Implementation story and lessons
entry.content:
When we think about electronic invoicing in Latin America, countries such as Brazil, Mexico and Chile often come to mind first. However, more and more organisations are expanding their operations into countries with newer mandates, where compliance requirements are equally important but implementation experience is still limited.

One of these countries is Paraguay, where electronic invoicing is managed through SIFEN (Sistema Integrado de Facturación Electrónica Nacional) under the DNIT (Dirección Nacional de Ingresos Tributarios).

At Origen Tech, we had the opportunity to help customers address this challenge by extending SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (SAP DRC) for Paraguay. Rather than building a standalone country solution, our objective was to follow SAP's strategy and leverage the extensibility of SAP DRC to deliver another country within the same global compliance framework.

For customers already using SAP DRC in multiple countries, this means continuing to build towards a common platform with one user experience, one compliance framework and one consistent business process worldwide.

Building on the SAP DRC framework

Our extension integrates directly with SIFEN/DNIT through SAP Integration Suite, following SAP's recommended integration architecture like for other countries in Latin America today. A future SAP-managed submission through SAP DRC Cloud Edition is considered in the future.

An important advantage of this approach is that customers do not require an additional third-party e-invoicing provider to communicate with the Paraguayan tax authority. The communication is handled through SAP Integration Suite, reducing architectural complexity and avoiding the additional licensing and operational costs often associated with external service providers.

The current outbound scope includes the electronic documents most commonly required by the Paraguayan mandate like: Domestic Invoice, Export Invoice, Credit and Debit Note, plus Remittance Note.

Because the solution is built as an extension of SAP DRC, it also benefits from the standard SAP monitoring, document processing and compliance framework already familiar to customers operating in multiple countries.

Every implementation teaches something

Every implementation is different, but after completing several project phases, some common success factors became evident.

The first is the importance of involving the customer's functional and tax teams from the beginning of the project. Electronic invoicing is much more than a technical integration; understanding the legal requirements and business processes early significantly reduces project risk.

Another key factor is collaboration. Projects progress much more smoothly when customer and consulting teams work as a single team, sharing knowledge and making decisions together rather than working in isolation.

We also learned that infrastructure readiness should never be underestimated. Components such as SAP Integration Suite need to be licensed, provisioned and available before implementation activities begin. Delays in platform availability can quickly become critical path items and impact the overall project schedule.

Finally, early access to development, quality and production environments—and visibility into the customer's onboarding activities with SIFEN—provides valuable opportunities to identify issues long before go-live.

These may appear to be standard project management recommendations, but one particular experience reminded us that even the best preparation cannot eliminate every implementation risk.

When production behaves differently from testing

Throughout the implementation, our integration testing was performed successfully using the Synchronous Web Service provided by SIFEN's test environment.

The results were consistently positive.

Multiple testing cycles were completed successfully, electronic documents were validated correctly, and there was every indication that the solution was ready for production.

After completing the technical cutover, the customer submitted the first live electronic invoices.

Unexpectedly, the documents were rejected during the authorisation process.

At first, nothing suggested a configuration issue. The same integration had worked flawlessly throughout the testing phase.

After working closely with SIFEN, we discovered the real cause.

Although the Synchronous Web Service is fully available in the test environment, the customer's production profile required communication through the Asynchronous Web Service.

This behaviour is not explicitly documented in the publicly available technical documentation. Instead, it depends on the taxpayer profile configuration and the internal technical architecture of the SIFEN production environment. As a result, there was no indication during testing that production would behave differently.

The situation required a last-minute modification to our communication architecture. Fortunately, because the solution had been designed with flexibility in mind, the necessary changes were implemented quickly, allowing the customer to resume electronic invoice authorisation with minimal disruption.

The real lesson

Looking back, this experience reinforced an important principle.

Successful testing does not always guarantee identical production behaviour.

No matter how many testing cycles are completed, some production-specific characteristics only become visible once the solution is processing live business transactions.

What ultimately determines the success of an implementation is not only the quality of the design or the number of tests performed, but also the team's ability to analyse unexpected situations, respond quickly and adapt the solution without compromising compliance or business continuity.

Conclusion

Paraguay continues to be an important addition to SAP's global electronic invoicing landscape.

By extending SAP Document and Reporting Compliance and integrating directly with SIFEN/DNIT through SAP Integration Suite, organisations can manage Paraguayan electronic invoicing within the same compliance framework they already use for other countries—without introducing additional third-party communication platforms.

Our implementation experience also demonstrated that technical expertise goes beyond delivering a working solution. It includes anticipating challenges, learning from production environments and continuously improving the solution based on real-world experience.

Hopefully, these lessons help other SAP practitioners preparing for their own SAP DRC implementation journey in Paraguay.

entry.title: Determination of electronic document processes in France with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance
entry.content:
France’s e-invoicing and e-reporting mandate introduces a layered set of rules for enabling invoicing compliance — whether that’s a B2B flow through the Approved Platform (Plateforme Agréée - PA), a B2G flow through Chorus Pro, or an e-reporting flow. This blog walks through how SAP Document and Reporting Compliance determine the correct electronic document type and process for the different scenarios.

 

 

Domestic Customer Invoices - SAP S/4HANA and S/4HANA Cloud

Key master data: what you need to set up first

Before the system can route any invoice, it needs to know the customers and how they are registered in the French directory (Annuaire).  The following business partner master data are used:

    • Tax numbers:
    • FR2 - SIREN – The main company identifier. This is mandatory — a VAT registration number alone is not sufficient.
    • FR1 - SIRET – The establishment-level identifier.
    • Identification numbers:
    • FRADLC (Addressing Line / Suffix) – An addressing suffix used when a customer routes invoices to a specific sub-entity identified by a suffix rather than a full SIRET.
    • FRROCO (Routing Code) – An additional routing attribute used in combination with SIRET for more granular routing.

These fields drive both the receiver ID used in the invoice and the process determination logic described below.

Receiver ID: which identifier is used to address the invoice?

The receiver ID is the key to identify where the invoice should be sent to. SAP determines it based on which combination of master data fields is populated.

If you maintain both SIREN and SIRET, you can control which one is used on invoices using the tax registration status.

      • PRA - B2B and active in the directory
      • PRI - B2B but inactive in the directory
      • PUA - B2G and active in the directory
      • PUI - B2G but inactive in the directory
      • NOR – Not in the directory

If both SIREN and SIRET are maintained as active in the directory, SIREN_SIRET is used.

▎Note: SAP Help documentation: link.

Additional identification numbers are used as follow:

      • If both Suffix (FRADLC) and Routing Code (FRROCO) are populated: SIREN_SUFFIX (suffix has priority) is used as receiver ID.
      • If Suffix (FRADLC) is populated and Routing Code (FRROCO) is empty: SIREN_SUFFIX is used as receiver ID.
      • If Routing Code (FRROCO) is populated and Suffix (l FRADLC) is empty: SIREN_SIRET_ROUTINGCODE is used as receiver ID.

Process Determination

The electronic document type is determined through the standard cross-country configuration table T003EDOCV. When the system determines document type FRB2BINV, it then runs additional logic based on business partner master data to decide whether the invoice should flow through the B2B/e-reporting channel (via PA) or the B2G channel (Chorus Pro).

  1. SIRET is checked first:
    • If the status is either Public Entity Active or Public Entity Inactive, e-document FR_B2BINV is not created.
    • If the status is Private Entity Active, configurations EDOFRPROCTVTAV (SD and settlement management) and EDOFRPROCT003V (SD, FI and MM self-billing) are checked:
      1. If no configuration found, e-document for B2B domestic invoice is created.
      2. If any configuration is maintained, e-document for either B2B domestic invoice or B2C (source for e-reporting) is created accordingly.
  2. If no SIRET, or SIRET has status Private Entity Inactive or Not Registered or no status, SIREN is checked.
    • If SIREN has status Private Entity Active or no status, configurations EDOFRPROCTVTAV (SD and settlement management) and EDOFRPROCT003V (SD, FI and MM self-billing) are checked.
      1. If no configuration found, e-document for B2B domestic invoice is created.
      2. If any configuration is maintained, e-document for either B2B domestic invoice or B2C (source for e-reporting) is created accordingly.
    • If SIREN has status Private Entity Inactive or Not Registered, e-document for B2C (source for e-reporting) is created.
  3. If no SIRET and no SIREN, e-document for B2C (source for e-reporting) is created.

If SIRET status is Public Entity Active or Inactive, or there is no SIRET and SIREN status is Public Entity Active or Inactive, no e-document for processing through PA flow is created. Electronic document for B2G is created depending on table EDOEUBUPAV.

 ▎Note: For SD documents, the partner function maintained in EDOCMSLSORGPF is used to check the business partner master data for process determination. If no configurations maintained, Bill-To part (RE) is used.

▎Note: If you have domestic sales to public entities (B2G), you do not need to set up e-document type FR_EUINV in T003EDOCV — this type is determined automatically if the customer is maintained in EDOEUBUPAV. For SD documents, the partner function in EDOCMSLSORGPF is used to determine the process.

 

 

Domestic Customer Invoices - SAP ERP

Key master data: what you need to set up first

SAP ERP uses a slightly different master data model.

      • Tax Number 2 is used to store SIREN. When populated, SIREN is considered active.
      • Tax Number 1 (even if it contains SIRET) is not used for routing.
      • SSF addresses are used to manage additional identifiers:
        • FRADLC stores either SIRET or the addressing suffix
        • FRROCO stores the routing code.
      • Public entity status is determined by the EDOEUBUPAV table entry, not the directory status field.

Receiver ID and process determination

      • FRADLC and FRROCO both empty → Tax Number 2 (SIREN) used. B2B e-document is created.
      • FRADLC maintained → SIREN + FRADLC used (SIREN_SIRET or SIREN_SUFFIX). B2B e-document is created.
      • Both FRADLC and FRROCO maintained → SIREN_SIRET_ROUTINGCODE used (FRADLC must contain SIRET, no system check). B2B e-document is created.
      • FRROCO maintained, but FRADLC empty → Invalid setup. System falls back to Tax Number 2 (SIREN).

If no SIREN is maintained, e-document for B2C e-reporting is created.

▎Note: SAP Help documentation: link.

 

 

Domestic Customer Invoices to One-Time Customers

For invoices posted to one-time customer accounts, the identifiers are entered at posting time rather than in the master data:

      • B2B invoice to be sent at SIREN level: populate Tax Number 2 during invoice posting. If SIRET is populated in Tax Number 1 is ignored.
      • B2B invoice to be sent at SIREN_SIRET or SIREN_SUFFIX level: populate Tax Number 2 (master data during invoice posting) and long text FRAD (addressing line code) at posting. Invoice is sent to SIREN_SIRET or SIREN_SUFFIX. There is no system-driven validation, if you populate FRAD including SIRET_ROUTINGCODE, SIREN_SIRET_ROUTINGCODE is used.
      • B2B invoice to be sent at SIREN_SIRET_ROUTINGCODE level: populate Tax Number 2 (master data during invoice posting) and long texts FRAD (SIRET) and FRRC (routing code) at posting. All three fields are concatenated.

If SIREN is populated, the invoice is treated as B2B. If SIREN is absent, it is processed as B2C/e-reporting.

▎ Note: this logic is the same for SAP S/4HANA Cloud, SAP S/4HANA and SAP ERP.

 

 

Self-Billing Invoices

MM Self-Billing Invoices

MM self-billing e-documents are created only if configuration table EDOINVVERV is populated with e-document types FR_B2BINV and FR_B2BCRE.

If the invoice belong the ERS (Evaluated Receipt Settlement) process, process FRSSBINV and e-document type FR_B2BINV are used.

If ERS is not set up (even if EDOINVVERV is populated) or EDOINVVERV is not populated, no e-document is created.

▎ Note: the check on ERS flag is not yet released.

FI Self-Billing Invoices

Process FRSSBINV is determined based on document type configuration in T003EDOCV. This means you need to use a dedicated document type to be able to leverage standard solution.

 

 

Non-Domestic (International) Invoices for E-Reporting

When the business partner country is not France, postings are considered for e-reporting when the document type is set up in T003DOCV with e-document type FR_B2BINV, or when no entry exists in T003DOCV at all.

▎Note: For SD documents, the partner function maintained in EDOCMSLSORGPF is used to determine the process. If no configurations maintained, Bill-To party (RE) is used.

The system uses two configuration tables to determine whether the transaction is in scope for e-reporting:

      • EDOFRPROCTVTAV – Applicable to SD and settlement management. It determines process based on Sales Organization, Distribution Channel, and Division.
      • EDOFRPROCT003V – Applicable to SD, FI, and MM self-billing. It determines process based on Document Type and Tax Code.

Based on the configurations maintained, the system determines the e-document for either B2B international or B2C.

      • B2C: Process FRIVREPSRC, e-document type FR_B2CINV
      • B2B International:
        • If account type K (vendor): Process FRIVREPSRC, e-document type FR_B2BSEU.
        • Otherwise process FRIVREPSRC, e-document type FR_B2BINVI. 

If no configuration is maintained: the document is considered out of scope for e-reporting. No e-document is created.

▎ Note: The following regions are treated as internation: 973  Guyane, 976 Mayotte, 988 New Caledonia, 987  French Polynesia, 977 Saint Barthelemy, 978  Saint Martin, 975 Saint-Pierre-et-Miq.

 ▎Note: Countries Guadeloupe, Martinique and Reunion are treated as domestic invoices.

 

 

Invoice Type Code Determination

The invoice type code is determined based on configuration table EDOCMINVTYPECODV.

Two enhancements are planned (not yet delivered):

      • When MM self-billing supplier invoices are posted with the same document type of standard supplier invoices (e-document process is FRSSBINV), you can configure EDOCMINVTYPECODV for standard invoices (e.g. 380), the system is planned to automatically map the code to 389 (invoice) or 261 (credit note).
      • In MM, supplier invoices and credit notes are posted with the same document type. You can configure EDOCMINVTYPECODV for standard invoices (e.g. 380) and credit notes are planned to be automatically mapped to 381.

 

Understanding this logic — and ensuring your master data is correctly maintained — is the foundation for a successful go-live.

entry.title: From Configuration to Compliance: Setting Up First Nations Tax Determination in SAP S/4HANA Cloud
entry.content:
The Report Is Ready — Is Your Configuration?

A companion blog post announced that the First Nations Tax (FNT) return is now available in SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (DRC) for SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud. That report gives Canadian businesses a structured way to file their FNT obligations — but the report only surfaces meaningful data when the sales pricing procedure is correctly configured to trigger and calculate the FNT in the first place.

This post focuses on exactly that: the configuration approach we recommend to ensure your sales documents carry the right tax determination for First Nations sales, so the SAP Document and Reporting Compliance report reflects accurate data when you run it. The setup described here is our recommended example — customers are free to adapt it to their own business needs, as long as the core mechanism for identifying First Nations locations remains in place.

 

Understanding the CTXJ Condition Type

In SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud, the tax jurisdiction trigger condition for Canada within the Sales and Distribution (SD) pricing procedure is CTXJ. It works the same way UTXJ does for the United States — it is a statistical condition in the SD pricing procedure whose job is to determine the correct tax code based on the customer's location and tax classification.

A few important facts about CTXJ:

  • It is used exclusively for Canada. The CTXJ access sequence (also named CTXJ) is only assigned to this condition type.
  • It must be defined as tax category with sequence 1 for the departure country CA (Canada) in the SD configuration.
  • It does not post to Financial Accounting directly. It passes the resolved tax code to the FI-relevant tax condition types (for example, CTX1, CTX2, CTX3), which carry the actual rates.

When a sales order or billing document is processed for a Canadian customer, the system evaluates the CTXJ condition to identify the applicable tax code — and that tax code determines whether FNT applies.

 

Extending the CTXJ Access Sequence

The standard CTXJ access sequence contains three accesses evaluated in order:

Access

Table

Key Fields

8

078

Departure Country / Destination Country

10

040

Country / State (Province) / Customer Classification 1 / Material Classification 1

20

002

Domestic Taxes

 

To support First Nations Tax determination, a new access must be inserted between access 8 and access 10. The core requirement for this new condition table is that it includes Transportation Zone as a key field. This is what allows the system to identify that a ship-to location falls within a First Nations reserve and apply the FNT tax code accordingly.

Our recommended combination for this new condition table is:

Country / State (Province) / Customer Classification 1 / Material Classification 1 / Transportation Zone

This is our recommended example — not the only valid approach. Customers are free to design the condition table to match their own business requirements. A simpler combination such as Country / Transportation Zone alone is equally valid, and the use of custom fields is also an option. What matters is that Transportation Zone is present, as it is the field that carries the FNT location identification.

Because the CTXJ access sequence is only used by the CTXJ condition type and is Canada-specific, any table you add here is isolated and does not affect tax determination in any other country or pricing procedure.

 

Mapping Locations to Transportation Zones (SSCUI 107364)

The Transportation Zone is the mechanism that tells the system a given ship-to location falls within a First Nations reserve. You configure this mapping using:

SSCUI 107364 — Map Location to Transportation Zone for First Nations Tax

This activity lets you assign a Transportation Zone to specific customer locations (typically identified by country and region/postal code combinations). When a sales order is created with a ship-to that matches one of these assignments, the system populates the Transportation Zone in the pricing communication structure, allowing the new CTXJ access to find the correct condition record.

SAP delivers example Transportation Zone values as part of the standard content. If you need to adapt these to reflect your business reality — for example, adding reserves that are relevant for your customers — you can do so using:

SSCUI 102362 — Define Transportation Zones

This Self-Service Configuration UI (SSCUI) is customer-modifiable, so your team can maintain the Transportation Zone values without requiring a development request.

 

Maintaining Condition Records for CTXJ

Once the access sequence is extended and the Transportation Zone mapping is in place, the final step is to maintain condition records for CTXJ using transaction VK11 (or the equivalent SAP Fiori app for condition record maintenance).

The fields in each condition record correspond directly to the key fields of the condition table you defined. If you followed our recommended example, each record combines:

  • Country (CA)
  • Region/State (the relevant province or territory)
  • Customer Tax Classification 1 (identifies whether the customer is taxable, exempt, or a reseller)
  • Material Tax Classification 1 (identifies whether the product is subject to FNT)
  • Transportation Zone (the First Nations reserve zone defined in SSCUI 107364)

If you chose a different table design — for example, Country / Transportation Zone only — your condition records will reflect those fields instead. The principle is the same regardless of the combination: the system matches the values on the sales document against the condition records and resolves to a tax code.

That tax code carries the FNT rate and the account key assignments that post correctly to your FI tax accounts — and, critically, it is the data that SAP Document and Reporting Compliance reads when generating the FNT return.

Without condition records for this access, the system falls through to the generic domestic access (table 002) and FNT is never calculated.

 

Next Steps

With this configuration in place, run an end-to-end test using a sales order with a ship-to assigned to a First Nations Transportation Zone. Verify that the CTXJ condition resolves to the expected FNT tax code, check that the billing document posts the correct tax amount, and then run the FNT report in SAP Document and Reporting Compliance to confirm the figures appear as expected.

The approach described here is what our team recommends as a starting point. Your implementation may call for a different condition table design, additional classification fields, or a simplified key — and that is perfectly valid. As long as Transportation Zone is part of the access, the FNT identification logic will work.

If you have not yet set up the DRC report itself, the companion blog post linked at the top of this article walks through that part of the process.

Questions about this configuration — or a different approach you found effective in your own implementation — are welcome in the comments below.

entry.title: French E-Invoicing using SAP DRC Cloud Edition
entry.content:
French e-invoicing and e-reporting reform introduces mandatory digital invoice exchange and transaction reporting through approved platforms. For large and mid-sized businesses, the key milestone is 1 September 2026, when domestic B2B e-invoice issuance and e-reporting obligations begin, while all taxpayers must be able to receive e-invoices.

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (SAP DRC) Cloud edition provides a framework to the companies and governments to  classify their AR/AP transactions into B2B, B2C, Cross Border etc. transactions and create the electronic documents for the billing issued to the customers , exchange invoices through Peppol-enabled access points, and report required invoice and payment data to the French authorities.

This knowledge article consolidates practical implementation considerations from my SAP DRC experience across Middle East and European deployments, with a particular focus on France.

It first establishes the regulatory and classification context, then moves into master data prerequisites, billing scenarios, Peppol routing, e-reporting, payment reporting, and implementation controls.

1. Purpose and Scope:

The purpose of this document is to provide a practical implementation guide for France e-invoicing and e-reporting using SAP DRC. It focuses more on Accounts Receivable than Accounts Payable, Account payable related knowledge article will be released soon. This document emphasizes on transaction classification, master data prerequisites, SAP-native billing, non-SAP billing integration, Peppol access point routing, and payment e-reporting.

With that scope established, the next section defines the intended audience and the assumptions that should be confirmed before the solution design is finalised.

2. Audience and Assumptions:

This guide is intended for SAP functional consultants, solution architects, finance transformation teams, tax compliance stakeholders, integration specialists, and project teams responsible for implementing France e-invoicing and e-reporting with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance.

I assume that the readers of this knowledge article have a working understanding of SAP S/4HANA or SAP ECC billing and accounting processes, business partner master data, tax registration concepts, and the role of SAP DRC in electronic document processing.

System assumption: SAP DRC cloud edition is available and activated for the relevant company codes and France compliance scenarios.

  • Master data assumption: Customer master contains the required country key, VAT ID, SIREN, SIRET 
  • Integration assumption: Any non-SAP billing systems can provide compliant XML invoice data for SAP DRC to create an e-Document using some middleware.
  • Regulatory assumption: Implementation decisions are aligned to the latest France e-invoicing and e-reporting requirements applicable at the time of deployment.

These assumptions provide the foundation for the regulatory overview that follows, where the core distinction between e-invoicing and e-reporting is introduced.

3. Regulatory and Solution Overview:

France’s mandate separates domestic B2B e-invoicing from e-reporting obligations. Domestic B2B invoices between parties established in France are handled as e-invoices. B2C transactions, international B2B transactions, and certain payment data are handled through e-reporting.

In SAP DRC solution, this distinction is primarily driven by business partner attributes which embeds critical combination of Country key, SIREN/SIRET ID & VAT ID.

From an Accounts Receivable perspective, SAP DRC supports three main France compliance flows:

  1. Electronic Invoicing (for Domestic B2B Sales)
  2. Electronic Reporting (for B2B International Sales and B2C Sales)
  3. Payment e-reporting for payments received from B2C and international B2B billing.

From an Accounts Payable perspective, SAP DRC supports inbound e-document processing and related reporting flows:

  1. Generation or receipt of e-documents.
  2. Processing of inbound e-documents into AP invoices using inbound AP automation.
  3. E-reporting for international B2B acquisitions of goods.

The French e-Invoicing mandate states below criteria for the application of e-Invoicing and e-Reporting to the companies.

Hence from 1st September 2026, E-Invoicing will become mandatory for Large and Intermediate Size companies as per the criteria mentioned in above screenshot.

4. Transaction Classification Rules:

The classification of a transaction as e-invoicing or e-reporting depends primarily on the BP country Key and customer establishment status. Customer establishment status is determined by the presence of SIREN (FR2) or SIRET (FR1) in the identification tab of the customer master data

In SAP DRC, the country key for BP is derived from the country key in ADDR1_DATA-COUNTRY. 

For a domestic B2B customer in France, country key must be either FR  or one of its three French Territories 

GP-Guadeloupe
RE-Réunion
MQ-Martinique

Beside above , the BP must have SIREN or SIRET ID maintained .

5. French Domestic B2B E-Invoicing in SAP DRC:

From a French regulatory perspective, domestic B2B e-invoicing applies where both the seller and buyer are established in France, and the transaction is subject to French invoicing rules. If the seller is established in France but the buyer is not established in France, the transaction is not treated as a domestic B2B e-invoice; it is handled through e-reporting instead.

For the France-specific SAP DRC solution, customer establishment status is determined using the following key attributes:

  1. The country key must be France or an eligible French territory (GP, RE, MQ)  recognised by the French authorities.
  2. The business partner master data must contain an active SIREN/SIRET value as shown below.

Customer master data attributes used to support domestic B2B e-invoicing classification.

Customer master data attributes used to support domestic B2B e-invoicing classification.

If both conditions are met, SAP DRC treats the customer as a domestic customer for France e-invoicing purposes. Alternatively, SIRET ID can also be used to represent the Tax Regs status of the company as PRA, for a company to have SIRET, it is mandatory for it to have SIREN first.

5.1 SAP Key Master Data Attributes:

SIREN: A unique nine-digit identifier used by the French government to identify a registered legal entity. It acts as the legal identity of the organisation and remains with the entity throughout its lifecycle. In many cases, it is derived from the last nine digits of the French VAT registration number.

SIRET: A unique 14-digit establishment identifier for businesses operating in France. It combines the SIREN with a five-digit location code, allowing individual sites or establishments of the same legal entity to be identified.

The selling company code must have country key FR.  If the Seller country key is other than France e.g. GB or ES and it uses French VAT ID then it falls under plant abroad scenario. If such company sells anything to a French domestic B2B then it falls under E-Reporting umbrella. 

Company code and country configuration relevant to France e-invoicing scope.

Plant-abroad scenario: This refers to a company code with a country key outside France, such as Germany, Spain, or the United Kingdom, using a French VAT ID to supply goods to a domestic French customer. The solution has been released now and if a company having non-French country key using French VAT ID bills to a established Domestic B2B customer in France, invoice will be classified under E-Reporting.

After the master data and establishment rules are confirmed, the next design decision is whether the invoice is created directly in SAP or received from an external billing platform.

6. SAP-Native Billing and Domestic B2B Invoice Generation:

In the SAP-native billing scenario, the SD billing document is created in SAP and then used by SAP DRC to generate the corresponding France e-document. For a domestic B2B customer, the e-document is classified as a France domestic B2B e-invoice when the required company code, customer, and establishment attributes are met.

France Domestic B2B E-invoice from SAP Native Billing System

Once the e-invoice is created, the seller’s approved platform or access point submits the invoice to the buyer’s approved platform through the Peppol exchange model. In this implementation context, SAP DRC acts as the seller-side platform.

Peppol acts as the exchange network between the seller and buyer approved platforms. The complete structured invoice is transmitted to the buyer, while the required invoice extract is reported to the French Public Invoicing Portal or tax authority reporting layer. The main points to consider are:

  1. The buyer receives the complete invoice in structured XML format through the Peppol network.
  2. The French Tax authority PPF receives the required invoice extract, not the complete commercial invoice.
  3. If the invoice extract is rejected by the PPF, the seller is notified electronically.
  4. If the invoice is rejected by the buyer, the buyer’s platform notifies both the PPF and the seller electronically.
  5. Rejection may occur if a customer dispute, such as incorrect quantity, price, or amount.
  6. In the case of a Reject action, the lifecycle status is also transmitted to the French tax authority (DGFiP) as it is a legal mandate. For all other actions (Accept, Dispute, Suspend, Partially Accept), the status is communicated only to the sender access point, there is no legal obligation to notify the tax authority.

Where invoices are generated outside SAP, the same regulatory outcome must be achieved, but the data ownership and integration responsibilities shift to the external billing system.

If the recipient PA does not receive (acknowledge) the invoice, the status remains Accepted by Service, even if the document has already been transmitted via Peppol Network. To check whether transmission via Peppol Network was initiated, use the app Monitor Documents app (Peppol monitor) in the cloud edition. If any failure occurred, the document is in status Sending failed. Any issues with pushing recipient acknowledgements can also be investigated in the Monitor Documents app.

Following flow exemplifies above process.

French Domestic B2B SAP Native Invoices

France Domestic B2B Invoice for External Billing System

PPF Successful Acknowledgment of Invoice Extract

7. Non-SAP Billing and External E-Invoice Integration:

Some organizations operate satellite or non-SAP billing systems where sales invoices are generated outside SAP. The resulting billing data may later be replicated to SAP FI-GL or uploaded for accounting purposes. In these cases, SAP DRC should not be assumed to have access to complete SAP-native billing or customer master data.

This is one of the most trickiest part of whole implementation.

Where the actual billing document is generated outside SAP, the non-SAP system must create an XML invoice that is compliant with the required French UBL format and Peppol standards.

After the XML invoice is generated by the non-SAP system, it is sent to the seller’s platform, which in our case is SAP DRC cloud, as a UBL file. SAP DRC then ingests the file and creates the corresponding e-document based on the attributes provided in the XML.

Note :For non-SAP billing, the determination of whether the buyer is established in France must be implemented by the companies using SAP DRC cloud edition using the guidelines given in the OSS 3772370 - Electronic Invoicing for France via Approved Platform: Corrections - SAP for Me.  

Following process flow describes briefly the process below behind the generation of a billing document in non-SAP system and its replication to SAP DRC.

Non-SAP Billing for a Domestic B2B Customer

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

For SAP DRC to create a compliant E-Document for France, all external billing systems must generate an XML file using some middleware and then transmit this XML to SAP DRC Cloud.

Refer to SAP KBA 3414491 3414491 - Electronic Document Processing for France - Preparation of XML Format for External Data - SAP for Me & for the XML format required for external data integration. The KBA includes mapping guidance for France domestic B2B customer scenarios where non-SAP systems generate the invoice data that SAP DRC will ingest.

The two billing approaches therefore need to be viewed as parallel process flows that converge in SAP DRC for e-document creation, platform submission, lifecycle monitoring, and reconciliation.

08. B2C and Cross Border B2B E-Reporting:

If either the seller or buyer is not established in France, the transaction is generally outside the French domestic B2B e-invoicing scope and is processed as e-reporting. This includes B2C transactions and international B2B transactions, except where specific French territory rules apply.

SAP DRC determines B2C and international B2B scenarios using the following key attributes:

  1. B2C customer: A business partner with country key FR, GP, RE, MQ and SIREN/SIRET are absent
  2. International B2B customer: A business partner created as an organisation with a country key outside France, including EU and non-EU countries.

Certain French territories as given below also fall under the umbrella of E-Reporting hence if a customer is created with the country key belonging to any of these , the billing generated against such customer will always be classified as B2B International and go to E-Reporting.

09. B2C and B2B International Customer Scenario:

When a B2C customer is created and an SAP SD invoice is posted, SAP DRC classifies the invoice as a France B2C customer invoice when the customer country key is France, and the customer does not meet domestic B2B establishment criteria. If the country key is not France, the system will classify the invoice as a France international B2B customer invoice instead of a France B2C customer invoice.

B2C customer invoice example created from SAP billing.

SAP DRC e-reporting treatment for the B2C customer invoice.

Once the invoice has been classified and reported, payment receipt may create a separate reporting obligation, which is handled through the payment e-reporting process.

Following process flow briefly describes the E-Reporting using SAP DRC cloud for SAP Native invoices.

B2BI and B2C E-Reporting for SAP Native Invoices

10. Customer Payment E-Reporting

Payments received from B2C customers and international B2B customers are reported in the payment e-reporting section of the SAP DRC cockpit where payment reporting obligations apply.

When payments are posted against the relevant B2C or international B2B invoices, SAP DRC records the payment information in the e-reporting area so that the required payment data can be submitted through the compliance process.

Payment E-Reporting for French B2C or B2B Customer Receipts.

Note:

If a single payment clears multiple invoices, one electronic document is created per cleared invoice. For partial payments, each instalment creates a separate electronic document, but the customer invoice status is not updated until the invoice is fully paid.

11. Mandatory e-Document Statuses in France

There are 4 mandatory statuses for an electronic invoice to contain.

(Submitted, Rejected, Refused and Payment received).

12. Implementation Checklist

  • EU02 (cf-eu02) subaccount for France electronic invoicing in SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (DRC), cloud edition requires an explicit EU Access entitlement on your global account, refer to OSS note 3756677 - Unable to create a Subaccount in EU02 for DRC for France Electronic Invoicing via Approved Platform | SAP Knowledge Base Article
  • Confirm the legal entity and company code country keys for all French invoicing flows.
  • Validate customer master data, especially country key, SIREN, SIRET, and their status.
  • Separate domestic B2B e-invoicing from B2C and international B2B e-reporting scenarios.
  • Confirm whether billing is generated in SAP or in a non-SAP satellite system.
  • For non-SAP billing, ensure the source system can generate compliant UBL XML files with the required France attributes.
  • Define Peppol routing identifiers and access point registration strategy.
  • Test invoice lifecycle statuses, including technical rejection and business refusal.
  • Validate payment e-reporting for applicable B2C and international B2B scenarios.

Below link from SAP work zone highlights important and upcoming updates about the French E-Invoicing solution using SAP DRC Cloud edition. I visit it every day to gain latest insights.
Known issues and latest timelines for planned feature releases 

13. Peppol Access Point Determination

For e-invoicing, Peppol access point registration can be performed using different French identifier combinations, including SIREN, SIREN-SIRET, SIREN-SUFFIXE, or SIREN-SUFFIXE-ROUTINGCODE. The selected routing model should align with the organisation’s legal entity, establishment, and operational routing requirements.

For e-reporting, reporting is performed at SIREN level. This distinction is important when designing master data, routing logic, and reporting responsibilities across multiple French establishments.

With routing determined, the remaining scenarios focus on transactions that fall outside domestic B2B e-invoicing and must instead be managed through e-reporting. 

 Conclusion:

In summary, a successful France SAP DRC implementation depends on clear transaction classification, reliable master data, well-defined billing ownership, compliant XML integration for external sources, controlled Peppol routing, and disciplined monitoring of invoice and payment lifecycle statuses. I hope this blog you will help you all in understanding SAP DRC cloud edition use case for France Electronic Invoicing mandate.

entry.title: What Slovakia's 2027 E-Invoicing Mandate Means for SAP Customers
entry.content:
Slovakia has set its date. From 1 January 2027, if you are a Slovak VAT payer sending a domestic invoice to another business or to a public body, that invoice has to be a structured electronic document. The data goes to the Financial Directorate.

One piece of news first, because it changes what your options look like. SAP is now accredited in the Slovak jurisdiction and appears on the Financial Administration's published list of accredited service providers. Slovakia is not building a central portal. Invoices travel through certified delivery services instead, so the provider you use has to be on that list.

ℹ️ Important info upfront:  if you want to see and hear how SAP plans to support, join us for the webinar on Sept 22 at 10 am CEST   ➡️ register here

What actually changes

The legal basis is the amendment to Act No. 222/2004 on VAT, which took effect on 1 January 2026. The e-invoicing obligation itself starts a year later, on 1 January 2027, and it applies to every VAT payer in the Slovak Republic.

From that date a PDF no longer counts. Invoices have to be structured and compliant with EN 16931, and Slovakia will use a CIUS in scope of the Peppol BIS 3.0 format.

There is one detail in the legislation that is easy to skip past. The recipient's consent for receiving an e-invoice may no longer be required. If your current process asks customers whether they accept electronic invoices, that step may simply fall away.

Two phases, not one

The reform is designed to replace the VAT Control Statement and the EC Sales List, but it does not do that immediately.

Phase 1 starts on 1 January 2027. Mandatory e-invoicing applies to domestic B2B and B2G transactions where the supplier is a Slovak VAT payer. Suppliers issue the structured invoice and report the data to the Financial Directorate. Everything outside that scope still runs through the VAT Control Statement and the EC Sales List, which stay mandatory.

That overlap is worth planning for. In 2027 you are running the new obligation and the old reporting side by side.

Phase 2 starts on 1 July 2030. E-invoicing becomes the default for all B2B and B2G transactions, intra-Community supplies included. The full real-time Digital Reporting Requirement goes live, and the VAT Control Statement and EC Sales List are repealed.

The three moving parts

1️⃣The electronic invoice is a structured document compliant with EN 16931.

2️⃣The delivery service is a certified service that transmits the invoice and reports the required data to the Financial Directorate automatically. This is the accredited provider layer, and it is what makes the Slovak model decentralised.

3️⃣The Digital Reporting Requirement (DRR) covers both sides of the transaction. Suppliers report, and so do recipients. Projects that scope only the outbound side end up doing the work twice.

Three things worth a second look

  • Input VAT deduction on domestic transactions may become conditional on holding a valid electronic invoice. That moves this out of the compliance box and into cash flow.
  • The deadline for issuing an invoice drops from 15 days to 10 days from the taxable event. This applies from 1 July 2030, not from 2027.
  • Invoices need new mandatory content, including the supplier's bank account details and, on corrective documents, a reference to the original invoice.

Where SAP delivery stands today

SAP plans to supports leveraging SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (link). For current planned delivery dates and scope, please refer to SAP Regulatory Change Manager, requirement GSREQEE-10396 for Slovakia (link: https://app.main.regulatory-change-manager.cloud.sap/index.html#/detail/GSREQEE-10396)

For planned timelines, please access tab ‘Product Impact’ and always refer back to this page for  updates. 

What's next for you

  • Check your product and release against the dates above.
  • Scope the inbound side as well as the outbound side.
  • Look at your partner and tax master data. Structured formats surface gaps that a PDF process never exposed.
  • Subscribe to RCM Slovakia Mandate GSREQEE-10396 so delivery changes come to you instantly. 
  • Come to the session: SAP is running a Slovakia readiness update on 22 September 2026 at 10:00 CEST. The session covers where delivery stands, how the phased rollout works in practice, and there is a live demo of SAP Document and Reporting Compliance handling the requirement end to end. It is recorded, so registering gets you the replay if the time does not work for you ➡️ Register here

Solution Brief https://www.sap.com/products/financial-management/document-reporting-compliance.html?pdf-asset=2221c... 

DRC Community https://pages.community.sap.com/topics/document-reporting-compliance

entry.title: What Global SAP Teams Get Wrong About Peru: SIRE Is Not Another Report
entry.content:
If you are running an SAP project with a Peruvian entity in scope, there is a good chance your compliance workstream is sized incorrectly. Not because the team is careless, but because the requirement looks familiar and is not.

I have spent the last two decades working on ERP projects in Peru, mostly from the quality assurance side — the person who comes in and asks whether what was promised is actually what was built. Peru's electronic books requirement is, by a wide margin, the item I most often find underestimated in project plans written outside the country.

The change nobody reads carefully

For years, Peruvian companies filed their accounting books through PLE (Programa de Libros Electrónicos). The model was simple and familiar to anyone who has done statutory reporting: the company generates a flat file from its ERP, validates it, and submits it to SUNAT, the Peruvian tax authority.

Your system is the source of truth. You produce the book. You send it.

SIRE (Sistema Integrado de Registros Electrónicos) inverts that.

Under SIRE, SUNAT builds a proposal of your Sales Register (RVIE) and your Purchase Register (RCE) from the electronic invoices already in its own systems. Each period, the company receives that proposal and must accept it, replace it, or complement it.

Read that again, because it is the whole point: the tax authority now arrives with a version of your registers before you submit anything.

 

Why this breaks project assumptions

When a requirement is written as "generate and submit electronic books", a project team scopes a report. Development effort, a test cycle, a sign-off.

But SIRE is not a report. It is a reconciliation process that runs every period, between what your SAP system holds and what the tax authority already believes. That difference changes several things at once:

  • It is recurring operational work, not a one-time build. Someone in finance owns a monthly comparison and a decision on every discrepancy.
  • It exposes master data quality immediately. A supplier tax ID that never caused visible pain now produces a line that does not match.
  • It moves the deadline. The work no longer ends when the file is generated. It ends when the differences are resolved.
  • It needs a defined owner. In more than one project I have reviewed, the requirement sat between the finance team and the technical team, and neither had written down who decides what happens when the proposal and the ERP disagree.

None of this is exotic. It is simply a different shape of work than the one the plan was built around.

Where SAP sits in this

SAP covers Peru through SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, and there is a leading SAP Note for the country that is the correct starting point for any scoping conversation. My recommendation is boring and I will make it anyway: read the leading note before you estimate, not after. The gap between what the standard solution delivers and what the local requirement demands is where project timelines quietly go.

A note on timing

The transition has not been a single date. SUNAT has moved it more than once. Most recently, R.S. N.° 000392-2025/SUNAT postponed the obligation for principal taxpayers with 2024 net income above 2,300 UIT from January 2026 to June 2026, while taxpayers below that threshold stayed on the January date.

If your program plan was built on a schedule published a year earlier, it is worth checking which group your entity falls into. I have seen a team prepare diligently for the wrong month.

What I would tell a project manager

Three questions, and you will know whether this requirement is under control:

  1. Who, by name, reviews the SUNAT proposal each period and decides on differences?
  2. What happens when the proposal contains a document your ERP does not have?
  3. Has anyone run a full period end-to-end in a test environment, or has the team only validated that the file generates?

If the third question has no answer, the requirement is not tested. It is formatted.

entry.title: Hungary's Move to eVAT M2M
entry.content:
Most of you know: Hungary is retiring ÁNYK. The General Form Completion Program stops being usable for the VAT return at the end of 2026, and from 1 January 2027 the return has to go through the eVAT system instead. If you file VAT in Hungary, the tool you have been using for years stops working in a little over three months.

But here is the silver lining: SAP has already shipped most of what customers need. That is unusual for a legal change of this size, and it changes the question from “when can I start” to “why have I not started yet”? 

One point that gets mixed up easily

From 2027 the eVAT system is mandatory. eVAT M2M is not.

There are two ways into eVAT.:

1) The web interface, where NAV generates a draft return from the data it already holds and you review and adjust it
2) Machine-to-Machine (M2) channel, where your system sends the VAT analytics as XML through NAV's API.

The web route is simpler and usually suits smaller businesses better whereas M2M is built for high transaction volumes incl. cross-border and intra-Community data. Most SAP customers running Hungarian entities land in the second group, but it is worth saying out loud that the mandate is eVAT, and M2M is the option you choose.

The dates that matter

  • 1 January 2026. New VAT return structures took effect, including the new return package and ESPL form releases.
  • 1 August 2026. The eVAT 2.0 schema went live. NAV published it in mid-May, earlier than expected, which left the rest of 2026 for testing.
  • 31 December 2026. ÁNYK is discontinued for the base declaration and for any reporting period after this date.
  • 1 January 2027. Data-based channels only. The eVAT web interface or M2M.

The A60 form for intra-Community transactions moves into eVAT as well, once its schema is published.

Where SAP delivery stands

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (link) is supporting customers for Hungary mandates. For current planned delivery dates and scope, please refer to SAP Regulatory Change Manager and select for SAP DRC and Hungary as country. (link: https://app.main.regulatory-change-manager.cloud.sap/index.html#/list=QWxs )

For planned timelines, please access tab ‘Product Impact’ and always refer back to RCM for current status of delivery and scope. You may also consider subscribing to the requirement to get notified of any updates instantly.

Two things that are easy to miss

  • The VAT coding has to line up with NAV's structure. This is usually where the work is, and it is a data and configuration exercise, not a technical integration one.
  • NAV changes the schemas. eVAT 2.0 arrived in 2026, and the cost of staying current is an ongoing one rather than a one-off project.

What is recommended now?

  • Check which SAP product and release your Hungarian entities run on, and match it against the delivery timelines in Regulatory Change Manager. If you are on S/4HANA in any flavour, the functionality is already there.
  • Decide between the web interface and M2M now, based on volume and on how much intra-Community activity you have.
  • Look at your VAT code mapping early. External advisers put implementation at one to two weeks for smaller companies and one to two months for larger ones, and most of that is data work.
  • Subscribe to Regulatory Change Manager and legal mandates listed for Hungary relevant for you to get notified instantly upon new updates  

Listen to SAP Experts

In a solution overview session for Hungary, local product managers of SAP Document and Reporting Compliance walk you through eVAT M2M process with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance: what the solution covers, how it works, and the steps to get ready. Here is the link to the recording and slides: https://event.on24.com/wcc/r/5462382/4AC703409D240B4C3B8FC7E2379B4DA3 (simply enter your email and the recording will start, PDF can be downloaded under additional resources section) 

More information: 
SAP Document and Reporting Compliance Page https://www.sap.com/products/financial-management/document-reporting-compliance.html 

Regional Collaboration workzones for Hungary (access can be requested via email registration): https://workzone.one.int.sap/site#workzone-home&/groups/request_access/5n2JnNilknl6rHima3dvZE 
Solution Brief https://www.sap.com/products/financial-management/document-reporting-compliance.html?pdf-asset=2221c... 

DRC Community https://pages.community.sap.com/topics/document-reporting-compliance

Regulatory Change Manager (filter for DRC and Hungary) https://app.main.regulatory-change-manager.cloud.sap/index.html#/list=QWxs 

 

 

 

Sources: SAP Regulatory Change Manager, requirement GSREQEE-3402 (Hungary, eVAT - VAT Analytics and Declaration with M2M Communication); SAP KBA 3719669; Act on Changes of some Tax Regulations LXXXIII of 2023; Government Decree 322/2024. (XI. 6.); NAV eVAT public repository and NTCA eVAT M2M guidance; Deloitte Hungary and WTS Klient commentary on the eVAT 2.0 schema and ÁNYK phase-out.

entry.title: Getting a Verification Code to Register Your Peppol Participant for Slovakia
entry.content:
Getting a Verification Code to Register Your Peppol Participant for Slovakia

Note: The steps and processes described here are accurate as of the time of writing, but it's essential to stay updated with any changes on the tax authority portal or the test tool for PFS that may affect this procedure.

If you are a Slovakian company and you use SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition to exchange electronic documents with your business partners and the tax authority, you must register a Peppol participant for your company as part of the setup. One of the prerequisites for creating this participant is a verification code. The verification code confirms that you have selected SAP SE as your certified delivery service provider, making SAP your access point in the Peppol network.

How you obtain the verification code depends on whether you use it for production or for test purposes. In this blog, you will learn how to obtain the verification code for both.

Obtaining the Verification Code for Production Purposes

For production purposes, you obtain the verification code by registering on the Slovak Financial Administration portal and selecting SAP SE as your certified delivery service provider.

  1. Open the tax authority portal at https://vpds.financnasprava.sk/.
  2. Navigate to the page listing the accredited service providers.
  3. Choose SAP SE as your accredited service provider and initiate the registration of your participant by selecting the corresponding action in the portal.

After the request has been successfully submitted, the Financial Administration sends a message to your inbox in the Personal Internet Zone (Osobná internetová zóna – OIZ). The message is titled Submission of a request for selection of a certified delivery service provider (Odoslanie žiadosti pre výber certifikovaného poskytovateľa doručovacej služby).

  1. Inside this message, copy the Verification data / verification code (Verifikačný údaj): <#EncryptedData#> and use it as the verification code when creating the participant for your company for production purposes.

Important: If you have email notifications enabled, the notification e-mail only informs you that a new message has been delivered to your Financial Administration mailbox. The verification code itself is not included in the notification email — you must open the message directly in OIZ to retrieve it.

Obtaining the Verification Code for Test Purposes

For testing your integration with the Slovak Financial Administration's test environment (tPFS), you generate the verification code yourself using a dedicated test tool.

  1. Open the Test tools for PFS (Testovacie nástroje PFS) at overtoken.sk/generate. The page provides tools for testing integration with the Slovak Financial Administration test environment (tPFS).
  2. Sign in by clicking Sign in (Prihlásiť sa). If prompted, continue using the configured Google account.
  3. Scroll to the section Generate a standalone verification token (data) (Vygenerovať samostatný verifikačný token (údaj)).
  4. Enter the Service provider TIN for SAP (DIČ poskytovateľa služby): DE143454214
  5. Enter your Entity TIN (DIČ subjektu — 10 digits).
  6. Click Generate verification token (data) (Vygenerovať verifikačný token (údaj)).
  7. Copy the generated verification token and use it as the verification code when creating the participant for your company for test purposes.

Next Step: Creating a Peppol Participant for Slovakia

Once you have the verification code, you can proceed to create a Peppol participant for your company in SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition. For more information, see Creating a Participant for Your Company for Slovakia.

entry.title: SAP DRC Cloud Edition para NF-e no Brasil: o que mudou em 2026?
entry.content:
SAP DRC Cloud Edition para NF-e no Brasil: o que mudou em 2026?

Em 2026, a SAP iniciou uma nova etapa na evolução de sua arquitetura de compliance fiscal eletrônico para o Brasil.

A nova integração de NF-e com o SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition, apresentada pela SAP em fevereiro de 2026, consolida o direcionamento para uma plataforma global de comunicação fiscal eletrônica.

Até então, os cenários brasileiros utilizavam serviços específicos, principalmente o SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, outbound invoicing option for Brazil e o SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, inbound invoicing option for Brazil, cada um com sua própria estrutura de onboarding, comunicação e operação. Markdown colado

Com o SAP DRC Cloud Edition, esse conceito muda.

A estratégia passa a ser a utilização de uma plataforma cloud global, preparada para suportar diferentes países, documentos eletrônicos, processos de compliance e participantes externos.

Mais do que uma atualização de infraestrutura, estamos diante de uma mudança de arquitetura.

1. De serviços específicos para uma plataforma global

Uma das principais mudanças introduzidas pelo SAP DRC Cloud Edition é a centralização da comunicação fiscal.

A SAP posiciona o Cloud Edition como uma solução global para comunicação e submissão de documentos eletrônicos, permitindo que diferentes países e processos utilizem uma infraestrutura comum.

Entre os principais benefícios desse modelo estão:

  • padronização da arquitetura de integração;
  • estrutura global baseada em SAP BTP;
  • utilização de contas e subcontas;
  • simplificação do onboarding;
  • expansão para novos países e cenários;
  • centralização dos serviços;
  • monitoramento mais centralizado;
  • direcionamento das novas funcionalidades para o Cloud Edition.

A estratégia é resumida pela SAP no conceito:

One Solution Scalable Worldwide

Ou seja: uma solução global que pode ser expandida para diferentes países e obrigações fiscais. Markdown colado

A nova arquitetura pode ser dividida em três grandes componentes.

Business System: representa o sistema responsável pelos processos de negócio e informações fiscais, como SAP ECC, SAP ERP ou SAP S/4HANA.

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition: representa a camada cloud responsável pela integração, troca de documentos eletrônicos, comunicação fiscal e monitoramento.

External Communication Party: representa os participantes externos, como SEFAZ, outras autoridades fiscais, plataformas governamentais, redes externas e parceiros de negócio. Markdown colado

Portanto, de forma simplificada, passamos a trabalhar com uma arquitetura:

SAP ECC / SAP S/4HANA
↓
Integration Steps
↓
SAP DRC Cloud Edition no SAP BTP
↓
Autoridades fiscais / SEFAZ / Parceiros externos

2. O SAP BTP passa a ter papel central na arquitetura

Uma das mudanças mais relevantes é que o SAP BTP passa a fazer parte diretamente da arquitetura da solução.

O Cloud Edition não é simplesmente um novo endpoint para onde o ERP envia documentos.

É necessário realizar o onboarding e provisionamento do serviço no ambiente BTP.

Isso envolve elementos como:

Global Account → Subaccount → Entitlements → Service Plans → Subscription/Service Instance → Usuários e autorizações → SAP DRC Cloud Edition

Essa camada passa a ser fundamental para o funcionamento da solução.

3. Ativação e onboarding do SAP DRC Cloud Edition no BTP

A preparação do Cloud Edition começa no SAP BTP Cockpit.

A SAP disponibiliza um acelerador para auxiliar na configuração da conta do SAP DRC Cloud Edition.

O processo guiado permite executar etapas como:

 

1. Iniciar o acelerador - O administrador inicia a configuração da conta para SAP DRC Cloud Edition.

2. Verificar os pré-requisitos - O próprio processo valida pré-requisitos como autorizações e direitos de uso necessários.

3. Selecionar o cenário - É possível trabalhar com a criação de uma nova subconta ou selecionar uma subconta existente, conforme a arquitetura definida para o projeto.

4. Configurar a subconta - Nesta etapa são definidos elementos como o plano de serviço e a subconta que receberá os recursos necessários. É importante destacar que a arquitetura deve considerar adequadamente os ambientes de Teste e Produção.

5. Adicionar usuários - São definidos os usuários e respectivos provedores de identidade e autorizações.

6. Revisar e executar - O acelerador executa as atividades necessárias, como atribuição de quotas, assinatura da aplicação, criação das instâncias de serviço e atribuição das respectivas autorizações.

7. Validar a configuração - Ao final, a subconta fica preparada para utilização do SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition.

Esse processo representa uma diferença importante na implementação: o onboarding da solução passa a fazer parte diretamente do desenho técnico do projeto.

4. Também existe a possibilidade de configuração manual

Além do processo assistido, os componentes podem ser preparados manualmente no SAP BTP.

De forma resumida, o processo envolve:

  1. criar a subconta na Global Account através do SAP BTP Cockpit;
  2. atribuir os respectivos entitlements, quotas e service plans;
  3. assinar/provisionar o SAP DRC Cloud Edition;
  4. atribuir usuários às Role Collections necessárias;
  5. criar a instância de serviço;
  6. obter as informações necessárias para integração com o Business System.

Essa possibilidade é particularmente importante quando o projeto exige maior controle da arquitetura BTP ou configurações específicas do ambiente.

5. Ativação do processo “Documentos fiscais eletrônicos (BR)”

Depois da preparação do ambiente BTP e provisionamento do Cloud Edition, é necessário habilitar o processo correspondente ao Brasil.

Dentro do SAP DRC Cloud Edition, o administrador acessa:

Configuração → Ativar processos e seleciona: Documentos fiscais eletrônicos (BR)

O processo inicialmente aparece como Inativo. Após selecionar Ativar, o sistema apresenta uma confirmação importante informando que, depois da ativação, o processo não poderá ser simplesmente desativado. Após a confirmação, o status passa para: Ativo

Essa etapa é importante porque habilita no tenant do Cloud Edition os recursos relacionados aos documentos fiscais eletrônicos brasileiros.

6. Um único ambiente de monitoramento no Cloud Edition

Outra evolução importante está no conceito de centralização do monitoramento.

No novo modelo, o SAP DRC Cloud Edition funciona como uma plataforma global para os diferentes processos suportados, permitindo uma visão mais centralizada da operação.

Em vez de pensar em soluções isoladas para cada país, o conceito passa a ser:

Uma plataforma global
↓
Diferentes países
↓
Diferentes processos fiscais
↓
Diferentes documentos eletrônicos
↓
Monitoramento centralizado

Isso é particularmente importante para organizações multinacionais.

Uma empresa pode evoluir sua utilização do DRC para outros países e obrigações fiscais utilizando a mesma estratégia global de plataforma.

No backend SAP continuam existindo os respectivos processos e ferramentas operacionais, como o eDocument Framework e EDOC_COCKPIT. Entretanto, a camada cloud passa a ser concentrada no SAP DRC Cloud Edition.

Essa distinção é importante: monitoramento centralizado no Cloud Edition não significa que o processamento de negócio do ERP deixa de existir.

7. Certificados digitais passam a ser administrados no ambiente Cloud Edition

Outro ponto fundamental da nova arquitetura é o tratamento dos certificados digitais.

A comunicação com as autoridades fiscais brasileiras depende dos certificados necessários para autenticação e assinatura, conforme o respectivo processo.

Durante a preparação do Cloud Edition, os certificados precisam ser disponibilizados e configurados no novo ambiente.

Portanto, a migração deve contemplar atividades como:

identificação dos certificados utilizados → exportação/preparação → validação da validade → validação da cadeia de certificação → carregamento/configuração no ambiente Cloud Edition → testes de comunicação.

Esse ponto deve fazer parte do planejamento desde o início.

Não basta configurar o ERP e estabelecer a comunicação com o BTP: o Cloud Edition também precisa estar corretamente preparado para se autenticar e se comunicar com as respectivas autoridades fiscais.

Isso também cria um novo ponto de governança.

A equipe responsável deverá controlar:

validade dos certificados, renovação, ambientes de Teste e Produção, empresas/CNPJs relacionados e configuração dos certificados no ambiente cloud.

8. SAP Note 3657680: ponto de partida técnico da implementação

Uma referência extremamente importante para a implementação é a:

SAP Note 3657680

Exchange of Electronic Fiscal Documents Using SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition – Leading SAP Note

A SAP Note 3657680 orienta a integração dos processos Inbound e Outbound com o SAP DRC Cloud Edition e funciona como uma Leading SAP Note para o cenário.

Ela reúne e direciona para as SAP Notes, correções, pré-requisitos e soluções necessárias para habilitar essa integração.

Por isso, eu considero essa Note um dos primeiros pontos que devem ser analisados durante o assessment técnico de uma implementação.

Em vez de começar aplicando notas isoladamente, a recomendação prática é utilizar a 3657680 como referência principal e, a partir dela, identificar as notas correspondentes ao release e cenário do Business System.

Como as SAP Notes podem receber novas versões, pré-requisitos e correções, é importante consultar sempre a versão vigente diretamente no SAP for Me.

9. Integração entre ERP e SAP DRC Cloud Edition

Depois da preparação do ambiente cloud, precisamos integrar o Business System ao Cloud Edition.

Esse é outro ponto importante da nova arquitetura.

A conexão exige configuração de comunicação e autenticação no backend.

Em um fluxo utilizando OAuth 2.0, por exemplo, temos atividades como:

1. Criar a ligação de serviço no Cloud Edition = A ligação disponibiliza os dados necessários para que o sistema de negócio consiga estabelecer comunicação segura com o serviço.

2. Obter as credenciais = As informações da ligação são utilizadas para configurar o cliente correspondente no backend.

3. Criar o perfil OAuth 2.0 no SAP ERP/S/4HANA = O backend precisa ser preparado para autenticação contra o novo serviço.

4. Configurar as credenciais e validar a autenticação = Somente depois dessa etapa temos efetivamente:

ERP ↔ autenticação ↔ Cloud Edition

Por isso, problemas de comunicação no novo modelo podem envolver diferentes camadas.

Um troubleshooting passa a analisar algo como:

Processo de negócio
↓
eDocument
↓
Integration Step
↓
Configuração do backend
↓
OAuth / autenticação
↓
SAP BTP
↓
SAP DRC Cloud Edition
↓
Certificado digital
↓
SEFAZ

Essa visão ponta a ponta será cada vez mais importante para profissionais que trabalham com DRC.

10. A migração precisa ser planejada como um processo controlado

Para clientes que já utilizam os serviços anteriores de NF-e do SAP DRC, a mudança não deve ser tratada simplesmente como uma alteração de endpoint.

O próprio conteúdo técnico do projeto evidencia uma sequência de preparação, configuração, validação e cutover. 

De forma resumida:

Preparação do Business System
↓
Análise e implementação das SAP Notes
↓
Preparação do SAP BTP
↓
Criação/configuração da subconta
↓
Provisionamento do SAP DRC Cloud Edition
↓
Configuração de usuários e autorizações
↓
Carregamento/configuração dos certificados digitais
↓
Ativação de Documentos fiscais eletrônicos (BR)
↓
Integração ERP ↔ Cloud Edition
↓
Configuração dos parâmetros específicos do Brasil
↓
Preparação dos processos Inbound/Outbound
↓
Testes
↓
Cutover

Existe ainda uma restrição importante: os serviços não devem permanecer ativos simultaneamente para o mesmo processo Inbound ou Outbound durante a operação. Markdown colado

11. Cuidados específicos com NF-e e CT-e Inbound

Para o processo Inbound, existe um cuidado adicional antes do cutover.

As consultas utilizadas na distribuição de NF-e e CT-e precisam ser corretamente tratadas antes da mudança.

Temos:

EDOC_BR_MNG_DISTDFE – NF-e

EDOC_BR_MNG_DIST_CTE – CT-e

Antes da mudança, os documentos pendentes precisam ser recuperados para o backend. O relatório EDOC_BR_DISTDFE_RETRIEVE pode ser utilizado nesse processo. O objetivo é chegar ao cutover com Total Documents = 0. 

Esse procedimento evita deixar documentos pendentes no fluxo anterior enquanto o novo ambiente começa a realizar as consultas.

12. O NSU precisa continuar do ponto correto

Outro detalhe técnico extremamente importante é o NSU – Número Sequencial Único.

Antes da desativação da distribuição anterior, o Updated NSU deve ser preservado.

Na configuração do novo ambiente, esse valor deve ser utilizado como:

Initial NSU

Portanto:

Updated NSU anterior → Initial NSU do Cloud Edition

Isso permite que a distribuição continue a partir do ponto correto, evitando descontinuidade na recuperação dos documentos. 

13. Ativação do Cloud Edition no backend

Depois que BTP, Cloud Edition, certificados, comunicação e processos estiverem preparados, chegamos ao ponto de ativação no Business System.

A configuração é realizada através da:

NFECE_SWITCHES – Atualizar funcionalidades de documentos fiscais eletrônicos

Os principais switches são:

DRCCE_IN – Ativar edição na nuvem para nota fiscal de entrada

DRCCE_OUT – Ativar edição na nuvem para nota fiscal de saída

Esses switches determinam quais processos passarão a utilizar o Cloud Edition. Markdown colado

Por isso, considero essa etapa o verdadeiro ponto de virada do cutover.

Antes de ativá-los, precisam estar validados pelo menos:

BTP → Cloud Edition → processo Brasil → certificados → autenticação → comunicação ERP ↔ Cloud → documentos pendentes → NSU → eventos → testes técnicos → testes funcionais.

14. O que não muda: o processo de negócio continua no SAP

O Cloud Edition não substitui os processos de negócio executados no backend.

No NF-e Inbound, por exemplo, podemos continuar tendo:

Recebimento do XML
↓
eDocument
↓
Validações
↓
Identificação do fornecedor
↓
Associação do Pedido de Compras
↓
Inbound Delivery
↓
Entrada de Mercadorias
↓
Invoice Verification / MIRO
↓
Contabilização

Portanto, precisamos separar claramente duas responsabilidades:

SAP DRC Cloud Edition: comunicação, integração e compliance eletrônico.

SAP ECC / SAP S/4HANA: processamento do documento e integração com os processos de negócio.

O eDocument Framework continua sendo fundamental nessa arquitetura. Markdown colado

Conclusão

A chegada do SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition para NF-e no Brasil representa muito mais do que uma alteração na comunicação com a SEFAZ.

Estamos falando de uma evolução para uma arquitetura:

global → centralizada → baseada em SAP BTP → padronizada → escalável.

O BTP passa a ocupar um papel importante no onboarding e provisionamento da solução; o Cloud Edition centraliza os serviços e o monitoramento cloud; os certificados digitais passam a fazer parte da configuração do novo ambiente; e a integração com o Business System passa por uma arquitetura própria de comunicação e autenticação.

Ao mesmo tempo, o eDocument Framework e os processos de negócio continuam no backend SAP.

Por isso, uma implementação precisa ser analisada ponta a ponta:

SAP ECC/S/4HANA → eDocument → Integration Steps → SAP BTP → SAP DRC Cloud Edition → certificados digitais → SEFAZ

E, para iniciar essa jornada tecnicamente, a SAP Note 3657680 passa a ser uma referência fundamental, reunindo e direcionando as SAP Notes e soluções necessárias para habilitar a integração Inbound e Outbound com o Cloud Edition.

Não estamos simplesmente mudando um endpoint.

Estamos adotando uma nova arquitetura para o SAP DRC.

Nos próximos conteúdos pretendo aprofundar as configurações do SAP DRC Cloud Edition para NF-e, incluindo SAP BTP, certificados, integração com SAP ECC/S/4HANA, NF-e Inbound, CT-e, eDocument Framework e troubleshooting de cenários reais de implementação.

entry.title: EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD BAdI Implementation for RESTRICT_CANCEL
entry.content:
The following blog post is relevant only for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Please note that Developer Extensibility is required.

 

Use case:

You are trying to cancel a Billing Document in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, but the system prevents it with the error message "Document XXXXXXXX: Unable to cancel document; Cancel related eDocument first". Alternative Use Case could be, that the cancellation of a billing document is allowed, but you want to further restrict it.

 

Important Warning:

This BAdI should only be used for special case handling allowing the cancellation or if you want to further restrict the cancellation. Please understand the country process in detail before overwriting standard country logic with the BAdI. If for example an eDocument is submitted and accepted by the authority, an invoice cancellations is often not allowed - the correction then has to be done with an additional document like credit memo or an additional invoice. Please keep also in mind that using this BAdI method can lead to inconsistent business data in your system - e.g. accepted eDocument with cancelled invoice. In many country implementations it is allowed to cancel the billing document, when the eDocument is in cancelled state or you were able to delete the eDocument.

 

Implementation:

To implement the above requirement method "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud~restrict_cancel" in BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD (enhancement spot ES_EDOCUMENT_CLOUD). The method “restrict_cancel” receives the edocument data in the importing parameter “is_edocument” and source key and source type. The changing parameter “cv_restrict” allows you to control whether the electronic document can be cancelled or not - the value which is handed over is the determined value by standard.

Implementation Steps:

  1. Create implementation for enhancement spot ES_DOCUMENT_CLOUD.
  2. Create BAdI implementation for EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD.
  3. (Optional) Create BAdI Filter for Country and/or Generic Filter.
  4. Create implementing class for BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD, which implements the interfaces "if_badi_interfaces" and "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud".
  5. Implement method "restrict_cancel" of interface "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud" in your BAdI class.
  6. Activate your BAdI implementation.
  METHOD if_edoc_adaptor_cloud~restrict_cancel.
      IF <your condition>.
        cv_restrict = abap_true/abap_false.
      ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.

entry.title: EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD BAdI Implementation for CHANGE_EDOCUMENT_TYPE
entry.content:
The following blog post is relevant only for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Please note that Developer Extensibility is required.

 

Use Case:

The Standard SAP eDocument Solution determines the eDocument Type with the values defined in "Assign eDocument Type to Accounting Document Type/Billing Document Type/Delivery Type/…". There are situations, were it is not enough to define eDocument Type based on the source applications document type. In those situations, you can use the BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD~CHANGE_EDOCUMENT_TYPE.

 

Hint:

Please search for notes before implementing this BAdI, if there is anything released. Sometimes, there is further customization possible to distinguish the eDocument Type. You could also check, if you can change your source application customizing to better distinguish.

 

Implementation:

To implement, use method "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud~change_edocument_type" in BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD (enhancement spot ES_EDOCUMENT_CLOUD). The method “change_edocument_type” receives the source data in the importing parameter “is_source_data”, "iv_source_key" and "iv_source_type". The changing parameter “CV_EDOC_TYPE” allows you to change the eDocument type which is selected for creation.

Implementation Steps:

  1. Create implementation for enhancement spot ES_DOCUMENT_CLOUD.
  2. Create BAdI implementation for EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD.
  3. (Optional) Create BAdI Filter for Country and/or Generic Filter.
  4. Create implementing class for BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD, which implements the interfaces "if_badi_interfaces" and "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud".
  5. Implement method "change_edocument_type" of interface "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud" in your BAdI class.
  6. Activate your BAdI implementation.
